# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 20 (Bu-Vb Pc20)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 20. Pouring water with living beings in it

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sappāṇaka Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 20) formulates the monastic rule prohibiting a Buddhist monk from pouring or sprinkling water containing living beings onto grass or clay [SuttaCentral; Harvey; Schmithausen 1991]. A monk who knowingly does so must confess the offense [SuttaCentral]. Analyzing culpability in the Vinaya, Peter Harvey observes that while inadvertence or ignorance that the water contains life incurs no offense, acting when one suspects or is unsure whether the water contains living beings constitutes a minor offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*), demonstrating that foresight or suspicion without direct killing intent carries culpability [Harvey]. Lambert Schmithausen notes that Pācittiya 20 and Pācittiya 62 (which forbids drinking water containing living beings) represent borderline cases under the broader precept against taking animal life, where the term *pāṇa* or *pāṇaka* specifically designates tiny animals or organisms [Schmithausen 1991; Bechert 1992]. In contemporary practice, monastic observance of this rule has included scrupulous inspection of water buckets before use to ensure no tiny creatures are harmed [Dhammika].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 20 and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 116, with parallel expositions preserved across the Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda traditions in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus reflects this shared transmission, showing substantial internal text reuse with other Theravāda Vinaya chapters—chiefly Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 62, Pācittiya 10, and Pācittiya 11—as well as cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* and Jayarakṣita's *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
